findings.title: DELETE statement uses sqlite-style placeholder despite MySQL-specific syntax
findings.evidence: The function explicitly targets MySQL DELETE ... LIMIT, but the executed DELETE binds the limit with a '?' placeholder. On supported POSIX Python deployments, common MySQL DB-API drivers use '%s' paramstyle, so this statement will fail at runtime when dry_run is false.
findings.recommendation: Use the placeholder style required by the actual database driver, or avoid parameterizing LIMIT if the driver does not support it and safely interpolate a validated integer batch_size instead. Add an integration test against the supported MySQL driver.

findings.title: Hard batch cap can leave matching rows undeleted while returning a normal result shape
findings.evidence: The loop stops after a fixed MAX_BATCHES and only then raises, meaning any cleanup with more than MAX_BATCHES * batch_size matches will commit partial deletions before failing. This is a reachable path for large tables and can leave retention cleanup incomplete after deleting up to 500000 rows by default.
findings.recommendation: Either make the cap configurable per call and surface partial-progress explicitly, or pre-count rows and refuse to start when the requested cleanup would exceed the cap. Consider wrapping the operation in clearer reporting so callers can distinguish partial deletion from complete success.
